Player
PLAY-er
n. (one who plays on a musical instrument)
From play, Old English plegian. In the Authorized Version a player is never an actor or a gamester but a musician, and the word appears at two of the most consequential musical moments in Scripture.

Biblical Definition

Saul's servants propose a remedy that brings David to court: “Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well” (1 Samuel 16:16). The search for a skilful player is the providence that carries the anointed shepherd into the king's house. The other uses are liturgical. In the procession psalm, “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels” (Psalm 68:25) — an ordered company with voice leading and instruments behind. And in the psalm of Zion's citizenship the players are placed in the city itself: “As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there: all my springs are in thee” (Psalm 87:7). Skill with an instrument is treated throughout as a real gift, sought out, employed, and set in the worship of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a player as one who plays; a musician; one who plays on an instrument of music; also, an actor on the stage.

expand to see more

PLAYER, n. One who plays in any game or sport.

PLAYER, n. A musician; as, a player on the lute or on the harp.

PLAYER, n. An actor of dramatic scenes; one whose occupation is to imitate characters on the stage.

CUNNING, a. Knowing; skilful; experienced; well-instructed; as, a cunning workman.

PSALTERY, n. An instrument of music used by the Hebrews, the form of which is not now known.

Key Scripture

1 Samuel 16:16 — "Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well."

Psalm 68:25 — "The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels."

Psalm 87:7 — "As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there: all my springs are in thee."

1 Samuel 16:23 — "And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him."

Modern Corruption

Musical skill in worship is treated either as performance to be admired or as a worldly intrusion to be resisted; Scripture sought out a cunning player, set players in the temple procession, and put them in Zion.

expand to see more

Two opposite mistakes crowd the subject. The first turns the player into a performer: the platform is a stage, excellence is applauded for itself, and the congregation becomes an audience. The second, in reaction, treats skill as suspect and prefers incompetence as though it were humility. Scripture supports neither. Saul's servants were told to seek out a cunning player, and God used that search to bring David into the king's house. The chronicler records instructors in song, men instructed and cunning, numbered and appointed. Skill is sought, trained and honoured.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition of the word itself. The principle to recover is the ordering in Psalm 68:25: the singers went before, and the players on instruments followed after. The voice of the congregation leads and the instruments support; when that order reverses, the people stop singing and start listening. And Psalm 87:7 gives the final dignity of the office — the players on instruments are not visitors to Zion but citizens of it, with all their springs in her. Music in the worship of God is not a concession to weakness but part of the city's permanent life.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew nagan (H5059), to play a stringed instrument; kinnowr (H3658), a harp; shiyr (H7891), to sing; chalal (H2490), to play the pipe.

expand to see more

Hebrew nagan (H5059) — to strike the strings, to play; the cunning player of 1 Samuel 16:16.

Hebrew kinnowr (H3658) — a harp or lyre; David's instrument before Saul.

Hebrew shiyr (H7891) — to sing; the singers who went before the players.

Hebrew chalal (H2490) — to bore, to play the pipe; the players of Psalm 87:7.

Hebrew maayan (H4599) — a spring, a fountain; all my springs are in thee.

Usage

"“Seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp” — skill sought deliberately."

"“The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after” — the order."

"“As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there” — citizens of Zion."
